Keep spot-removed-seam and flip the Checkpoint to the one-adapter case, keeping the id:
```checkpoint real-seam

- [x] One adapter: a hypothetical seam, so hold off.
  > Right. Nothing varies across it yet. Add it when a second adapter, such as a test fake, actually exists.
- [ ] Keep it: switching providers one day will be easier with it in place.
  > "One day" is still one adapter today. Add the seam when the second adapter really exists.
- [ ] Keep it: the name `EmailSender` makes the code read more nicely.
```

quiz.problem: The labels on the options give the answer away. The stem describes a maintainer's job (fixing a bug in one place), and the right option is the one labelled "which maintainers get", so a reader can match on the label without knowing what locality means. Options c and d aren't benefits of depth, so they don't fit the stem's "Which benefit of depth is that?". That leaves a two-way choice the label settles.
quiz.evidence: Line 378 stem: "fixing a rounding bug meant hunting through five files ... Which benefit of depth is that?" Line 39: "Callers get leverage ... Maintainers get locality". Option c "A real seam, since prices now pass through one spot" and option d "Depth in the implementation, since the module now holds more code" name a seam and a property, not a benefit.
quiz.fix:
Drop the labels and widen the stem so every option fits it:
```test why-locality
Before a deepening, fixing a rounding bug meant hunting through five files that each rounded prices their own way. Now there's one place to look and one place to change. Which word from the vocabulary names that gain?
- [x] Locality
  > Right. Change, bugs and checking now live in one place, so a fix there is a fix everywhere. It's what maintainers get.
- [ ] Leverage
  > Leverage is what callers get: more capability per thing they learn. This is about where a maintainer has to look and change.
- [ ] A real seam, since prices now pass through one spot
  > A seam is where adapters can be swapped. Nothing is being swapped here.
- [ ] Depth in the implementation, since more code sits inside
  > Depth is measured at the interface, not by how much code sits inside.
```

quiz.where: Final test spot-carried-on (line 317-327), stem "The agent then starts editing five files ... What should Sam have done?" (line 318) and d "Commit the HTML report first, so the edits can point back to it." (line 325)
quiz.problem: Three things are wrong. (1) Distractor d is weak: the Lesson says the report is a temp file outside the project, so it can't be committed, and nobody would pick d. (2) The tenses clash: the agent "starts editing" now, yet the stem asks what Sam "should have done", and option a "Let it finish" reads oddly against it. (3) The stem and the right option repeat the Common mistakes bullet a few lines above, so the question checks recall, not transfer.
quiz.evidence: Line 133: "goes to your computer's temp folder ... so nothing lands in your project". Line 241: "If the agent starts editing after you agree, press Esc. The Main flow builds the decision." Right option, line 321: "Stop it, and take the decision into the Main flow."
quiz.fix:
```test spot-carried-on
Sam runs the survey and, after two rounds of grilling, agrees with the top candidate. The agent then starts editing five files in the same session. What should Sam do?
- [ ] Let it finish, since agreeing with the candidate was approval to build.
  > Agreeing settles a design, not a go-ahead to build. The survey should end with a decision, not a code change.
- [x] Press Esc, and carry what was agreed into `/to-spec`.
  > Right. The Skill's job ends at the decision; building isn't one of its steps. A spec, then tickets, builds it.
- [ ] Ask it to do the other candidates too, while it has the report open.
  > One candidate per session. Several at once fill the context window with reports, grilling and edits.
- [ ] Let it finish on a new branch, so the main code stays safe.
  > A branch keeps the edits apart, but they're still a build nobody planned. The building comes later, through a spec and tickets.
```
